response.sql:
WITH per_rental AS (
  SELECT p.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.amount >= 4.99
  GROUP BY p.rental_id, i.store_id
)
SELECT store_id, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_rental_total, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental
FROM per_rental
GROUP BY store_id

assumptions.assumption: The 4.99 threshold is applied to each individual payment (amount >= 4.99) before totaling per rental, not to the per-rental totals.
Payments with NULL rental_id, or whose rental or inventory row doesn't exist, are dropped via inner joins.
